premises.text: Many couples need relationship help that fits everyday life; a substantial share find therapy ineffective and there has been no digital health-tracking solution
premises.evidence_span: 11 to 18 percent of people that go to therapy find it to be not effective. There is no digital solution

premises.text: LifeCouple uses a metric onboarding questionnaire and proprietary algorithm across communication, trust, intimacy, and conflict, then check-ins, alerts, and AI to close satisfaction gaps
premises.evidence_span: through a proprietary algorithm, four key areas of the relationship have now been filled. Communication, trust, intimacy and conflict

premises.text: The platform complements therapy and EAPs rather than replacing them, giving therapists measurable activities between sessions
premises.evidence_span: we complement therapy. We do not say that therapy is going to be replaced by technology

premises.text: Unlike competitors, LifeCouple tracks and monitors relationship health continuously
premises.evidence_span: no one tracks and no one monitors the health of one's relationship

domains.name: Therapy gap and everyday relationship need

value.text: Keep relationships healthy—a Fitbit for your heart
value.evidence_span: LifeCouple is a Fitbit for your heart

secondary_value.text: Reduce unproductivity from divorce and unhappy marriages in EAP contexts
secondary_value.evidence_span: 13 billion dollars is lost of unproductivity because of people divorced or in an unhappy marriage

causal_links.evidence_span: address relationship challenges in a way that's suitable for their everyday life
This platform was built to keep a relationship healthy

notes: Icebreakers, digital gifts, love languages folded into platform premise (§4.1(5)). CAC/user traction excluded. 'Future of relationship health' treated as vision framing not premise (§4.1(4)). Need/product/channel triad justified: therapy-complement GTM revisable without changing the algorithm, and therapy-ineffectiveness is a separate market claim.
